WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him

"In his days Pharaoh-nechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him." 2 Kings 23:29

Chronicles gives his message to Josiah: "What have I to do with thee, thou king of Judah? I come not against thee this day, but against the house wherewith I have war: for God commanded me to make haste". 2 Chronicles 35:21
Chronicles says Josiah "hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of God". 2 Chronicles 35:22
He bound Jehoahaz at Riblah, fined the land a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, made Eliakim king and "turned his name to Jehoiakim". 2 Kings 23:33–34
Jeremiah: "the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim". Jeremiah 46:2

"And the king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land: for the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt unto the river Euphrates all that pertained to the king of Egypt." 2 Kings 24:7
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Necho claimed a command from God; Chronicles calls his words "from the mouth of God". 2 Chronicles 35:21–22
Judah became Egypt's tributary under a king Necho chose: "Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh". 2 Kings 23:35
Jehoiakim "taxed the land ... of every one according to his taxation, to give it unto Pharaoh-nechoh". 2 Kings 23:35
"All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah." 2 Chronicles 35:24

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No regnal years. Scripture dates his deeds by Judah's kings: Josiah's death, Jehoahaz's three months, and Carchemish in Jehoiakim's fourth year (Jer 46:2).

"610–594 BC"; Nicol dates Megiddo 608 and Carchemish 604.
The king of Babylon, ruling Assyria's empire
Matthew Poole (1683–85); the Pulpit Commentary (1881)
"King of Assyria" means the Babylonian king, probably Nabopolassar. 2 Kings 23:29 [51][52]
The last king of Assyria
Ellicott's commentary; W. E. Barnes (1899)
Necho's enemy was the last king of Nineveh, then at war with Nabopolassar. 2 Chronicles 35:20 [54][55]
Cannot be determined
C. F. Keil (1872)
It depends on the year Nineveh fell, which Keil could not fix. 2 Kings 23:29 [53]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say why Josiah went out against Necho.
Scripture does not say whether Necho reached the Euphrates in the year Josiah died, or what he did there.
Scripture does not name Necho in the account of Carchemish outside Jeremiah 46:2.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Scholars' viewPharaoh-necho is identified with Necho II of Egypt's 26th dynasty, the Necos son of Psammetichos of Herodotus. 2 Kings 23:29 [17][6][21]
From the textThe person record also places under him "Pharaoh king of Egypt" in Jeremiah's oracle on Carchemish (Jer 46:17, 25), verses that do not name him. Jeremiah 46:17 Jeremiah 46:25
